raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-BFA-EconomicOpportunitiesResilience",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "High insecurity and ongoing conflict in target regions may restrict access to project locations, disrupt service delivery, and hinder direct field supervision.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Adopt adaptive implementation modalities, including remote monitoring via GEMS, third-party monitoring, remote delivery channels, and partnerships with local CBOs and NGOs.",
      "evidence": "high insecurity in some of the areas in which project activities will be conducted"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Targeting vulnerable populations in fragile settings creates a heightened risk of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, enforce strict codes of conduct, recruit a dedicated GBV/SEA/SH specialist, and set up a sensitive grievance mechanism with referral pathways.",
      "evidence": "SEA/SH risk is Substantial, reflecting the nature of project activities and the vulnerability of the target population"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "The implementing ministry currently lacks a functional PIU with established financial management systems, software, and World Bank project experience.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit qualified financial management specialists before effectiveness, acquire approved accounting software, prepare a financial procedures manual, and establish internal audit oversight.",
      "evidence": "The assessment found that the MFS currently does not have a PIU with FM arrangements in place"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Public administrative routines and multi-layered approval processes may cause significant procurement delays and impede implementation timelines.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Define maximum review and approval delays per procurement stage in the Project Implementation Manual and provide dedicated training to bid committees.",
      "evidence": "administrative routines may result in procurement delays, potentially affecting project implementation"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Procurement in fragile or insecure zones with limited active suppliers risks restricting market competition, inflating prices, and increasing collusion risks.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Apply flexible World Bank procurement procedures tailored for fragile situations and phase activity launches starting in accessible communes.",
      "evidence": "procurement in fragile areas with few bidders can restrict competition and possibly increase prices and collusion risks"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Insufficient technical capacity within the PIU and bid committees may result in weak contract administration and poor oversight of major procurement contracts.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit an experienced full-time procurement specialist, establish formal contract management plans in STEP, and conduct capacity-building workshops.",
      "evidence": "insufficient capacity can lead to poor contract management and administration of big contracts"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Civil works for constructing 28 warehouses and rehabilitating 10 regional centers could cause soil and water pollution and worker safety hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Screen subprojects using E&S procedures, prepare site-specific ESIAs/ESMPs, and mandate compliance with occupational health and safety standards.",
      "evidence": "key E&S risks and impacts include water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste at construction and rehabilitation sites"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Connecting the Unique Social Registry with national ID and payment systems creates data privacy and cybersecurity vulnerabilities regarding beneficiary data.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce national data protection laws under CIL oversight and adopt security and data-exchange protocols approved by the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI).",
      "evidence": "follow the security procedures elaborated by the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "The fluid national political environment in Burkina Faso may cause institutional shifts, policy changes, or governance bottlenecks during project execution.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Anchor project activities within the broader national PAMPV strategy and utilize the multi-sectoral Steering Committee to maintain institutional alignment.",
      "evidence": "the country's current fluid political situation."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Severe fragmentation across social protection actors and ministries risks creating coordination bottlenecks, operational overlap, and communication failures.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a functional inter-ministerial Steering Committee and formalize operational protocols and data-sharing frameworks across participating institutions.",
      "evidence": "Burkina Faso’s social assistance system is highly fragmented, with more than 200 interventions implemented by 50 agencies."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Flaws in targeting or social barriers could lead to the exclusion of marginalized groups, such as IDPs, women, youth, and persons with disabilities, from economic benefits.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize RSU proxy means testing combined with community validation assemblies, enforce gender quotas, and deploy an accessible Grievance Redress Mechanism.",
      "evidence": "exclusion from the project’s benefits of certain categories of people such as vulnerable groups including women, youth, people with disabilities"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Land acquisition or site clearing for warehouse construction and provincial intake center upgrades could result in localized economic displacement.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize available public land, screen all construction sites for resettlement impacts, and formulate Resettlement Action Plans or Livelihood Restoration Plans as needed.",
      "evidence": "ESS 5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement... economic displacement."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Delays in fulfilling post-effectiveness legal covenants, such as recruiting mandatory key specialists, could slow down overall project initiation.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Initiate recruitment processes early during preparation and closely track legal covenant compliance deadlines post-effectiveness.",
      "evidence": "The PIU shall include the following additional key staff... no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date"
    }
  ]
}
